overview: This two-page file links a cross-reference concerning Japanese dollar bonds held by the International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation with a memorandum of conversation about Shanghai telephone rates. The cross-reference records an affiliate’s request to return bonds to Japan aboard a Japanese steamer, while the memorandum reports that the Shanghai Municipality and French Concession had approved rate increases intended to offset losses caused by depreciation of the Chinese dollar.

people.name: Frank C. Page
people.role: Representative of the International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation

people.name: Mackay
people.role: Official of the State Department’s Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on return of Japanese affiliate’s dollar bonds
subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a memorandum concerning an ITT affiliate’s request for the return of Japanese dollar bonds to Japan by Japanese steamer.
subfiles.summary: The sheet records that Japanese dollar bonds belonging to the Japanese affiliate of the International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation were held in the corporation’s custody. The affiliate requested their return to Japan and sought expedited handling by Japanese steamer. Frank C. Page informed the Department by telephone, and the sheet directs researchers to the original memorandum in file 894.51/675.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation on increased Shanghai telephone rates
subfiles.from: Mackay, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Frank C. Page reports official approval of higher Shanghai telephone rates intended partly to compensate ITT for losses from Chinese-currency depreciation.
subfiles.summary: Following a discussion of another matter, Frank C. Page told Mackay that the Shanghai Municipality and French Concession authorities had approved an increase in telephone rates. The increase was expected to take effect around the middle of December and partially offset the corporation’s losses from the sharp decline in the Chinese dollar’s exchange value. Mackay thanked Page and said the information would be brought to the attention of the appropriate Department officers.

interest: The file offers a compact view of ITT’s financial and regulatory concerns in East Asia in late 1940, linking securities custody and wartime transportation with municipal telephone pricing and currency depreciation. It is especially useful for tracing informal corporate communication with the State Department and the divided administrative authority of Shanghai, where both the municipality and French Concession had to act on rate changes. The cross-reference also points researchers to a related original memorandum filed under a different decimal classification.
